questions.question:
Identify the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment. If no substitution is required, select No substitution.

All the accident victims have been admitted __and received__ attention.
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 2.**
 
• The given sentence is in Present perfect tense so the underlined phrase should also be in the present perfect tense. 
 
• Therefore, option 1 gets eliminated. 
 
• Option 3 is wrong because it is in the past perfect tense.
 
• Option 4 is wrong because it is in the present continuous tense. 
 
• **Therefore, the correct answer is 'and have received' which is in the present perfect tense.**

questions.question:

PITFALL
questions.solution:
**Pitfall: Potential problem, hazard, or danger.

(**The store fell into one of the major **pitfalls** of small business, borrowing from suppliers by paying bills late)

 
• Haven: A place of safety; a refuge or sanctuary.

 (The garden was a **haven** from the noise and bustle of the city.)

 Attacks by enemy aircraft forced the tanks to **retreat** (from the city).

**Therefore, out of given alternatives, the word 'hazard' gives the most appropriate meaning of the given word.**

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives

their correct order.

A. We even fail to recognize that their call of duty keeps them away from their families.

B. Yet, we often fail to appreciate these sacrifices that they make.

C. They make countless sacrifices for the nation and keep us safe from our enemies.

D. The uniformed men and women are our unsung heroes.
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 2.**
 
• The answer does not begin from sentences A, B & C because these sentences are beginning with pronouns(We, they) and conjunction(yet).
 
• The only independent sentence we have is D which is our first sentence.
 
• Sentence D is talking about two subjects i.e. 'men' and 'women'. Sentence C is beginning with a pronoun 'they' which refers to 'men and women'.
 
• Sentence C is talking about the sacrifices made by men and women which is continued by sentence B saying that we fail to appreciate these sacrifices. Sentence A beginning with 'we even fail to' shows that this is a continuation of sentence B.
 
• **This sequence of DCBA is given in option 2. **

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate indirect form of the given sentence.**

She says, "I go for a walk every morning."

options.text: She says that she goes for a walk every morning.
She says that I go for a walk every morning.
She said that she went for a walk every morning.
She said that she goes for a walk every morning.

questions.solution:
• When the **Reporting Ver**b is in the **Present Tense** of Future Tense, there is **no change in the Verb** of the **Reported Speech.**

 
 
• The given sentence is in **present indefinite tense,** hence, '**She says**' will **remain same** (not be changed into 'said to').
 
 
 
• If there is any **Universal Truth or Habitual Truth** in the **Reported Speech**, there is** no change **in the **Reported Speech**.
 
 
• The reported speech is a **routine action**, hence, it will **not **be **changed.**
 
 
 
• **PRONOUN change** - According to the First-Person=Subjective form, according to the Second Person=Object form and in Third Person=No change.)
 
 
• 'First-person' changes to the subject i.e. **'I' **changes to** 'she'.**
 
 
 
• Singular **"she"** will take **'s/es' **with its verb i.e. **'go'** **changes **to** 'goes'.**

 

**Therefore, this structure is followed in Option 1 'She says that she goes for a walk every morning'.**

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4) i.e. of the king's.**

• Because both 'of' and apostrophe are used to show possession, hence, **'the picture of the king' **will be used.
 
• So, the correct sentence will be: **The picture of the king is exactly like the king himself.**

questions.question:

His little brother's ball was thrown at him.
The ball is thrown towards his little brother.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2) i.e. the ball was thrown towards his little brother.**

 
• The given sentence is in the** past indefinite tense,** hence, while changing it into the passive voice, **was+thrown** will be used.
 
• And the object i.e. ball will be made the subject.
 
• All these rules are followed in option 2), hence, it will be the correct answer.

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.

A. As a result, he had gotten into a million activities and hobbies.

B. Thus, his parents were now reluctant to spend any more money on his hobbies.

C. John hated finishing things almost as much as he loved starting them.

D. But he never stuck with any of them for long.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1) i.e. CADB.**

 
• The only **independent sentence** from the given sentences is** 'C'**, hence, it will be the first sentence.
 
• So, options 2 and 4 cannot be the correct answer.
 
• The sentence, A, talks about the **hobbies **and in sentence D, the pronoun 'them' has been used for 'activities and hobbies'. This makes the **'AD' **a correct pair here.
 
• The word **'thus'** used in the sentence **'B'** shows the **conclusion**, hence, it will be the last sentence.
 
• So, the correct sequence is **CADB.**

questions.question:
Identify the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment. If no substitution is required, select No substitution.

The commander of the ship as well as the crew __are caught by__ the storm.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3) i.e. is caught in.**

 
• When two subjects are connected with **'as well as'** the verb always agrees with the **first subject**.
 
• In the given sentence, the first subject is **'the commander'** and that is a **singular** subject, hence, a singular verb i.e.** 'is'** will be used for it. 
 
• So, the correct substitution is **'is caught in'**.
 
• **Note**: other words with which this rule is followed are: unlike, along with, with, besides, in addition to, but, etc.
